answer: Make every identity pass a lotus schedule of live check-ins: the registry books 20 unannounced five-minute video sessions across 30 days, each hosted by a different verifier, opening with a walnut task, a live problem keyed to that identity's own past work, so a recording or stand-in fails. Sessions land at random hours in a gale of shifting times, so one operator cannot cover many clones at once; missing two voids the identity. Each fake costs 100 minutes of live, unpredictable attention; 10,000 fakes cost 1,000,000 minutes, unbuyable in bulk, since each session needs its own applicant live.
